eligibility_reason: Mostly new mechanistic experiments, but the authors explicitly reproduce their own published finding (Chen et al., 2014) with new postpartum rats: Exp 1 reports MK212 (2.0 mg/kg) disruption 'in agreement with our previous report (Chen et al., 2014)', and Exp 4 states 'we replicated the acute disruptive effect of MK212 on pup retrieval'. These are self-replications, which the codebook includes; eligibility is borderline because the replication is incidental to new research questions.

effects.original_title: Effects of 5-hydroxytryptamine 2C receptor agonist MK212 and 2A receptor antagonist MDL100907 on maternal behavior in postpartum female rats
effects.original_authors: Chen, W; Zhang, Q; Su, W; Zhang, H; Yang, Y; Qiao, J; Sui, N; Li, M
effects.outcome: Active maternal behavior, especially pup retrieval (number of pups retrieved, first-retrieval latency; also nursing, licking, nest building)
effects.timepoint: 30 min post-injection (disruption absent at 2 h and 4 h)
effects.description: Acute systemic administration of the selective 5-HT2C agonist MK212 disrupts active components of maternal behavior, especially pup retrieval, in postpartum rats (2.0 mg/kg producing the most disruption).
effects.citation_sentence: In agreement with our previous report (Chen et al., 2014), acute MK212 injection severely disrupted various active components of maternal behavior.
effects.evidence: Results 3.1: 'In comparison to the VEH groups, rats treated with MK212 retrieved significantly fewer pups (all p < 0.001) and took a much longer time to complete pup retrievals (all p < 0.001) at the 30 min post injection testing point under both the pup separation and no separation conditions'; main effect of drug on pups retrieved F(1, 58) = 113.679, p < 0.001. Discussion: 'maternal behavior, especially pup retrieval, was severely disrupted at the 30 min testing point after MK212 injection (2.0 mg/kg)'.
effects.notes: Self-replication (same lab: Li M is senior author of both; Methods 2.3: 'The basic procedure was identical to what has been described in our previous studies (Chen et al., 2014...)'; dose chosen because it 'produces a reliable disruption on maternal behavior (Chen et al., 2014)'). Embedded in a new crossover design adding pup separation; the no-separation arm is the closest reproduction, but the drug main effect holds in both arms. Licking was not significant in the no-separation condition (p = 0.107) while retrieval, nursing and nest building were all p < 0.001; treated as measures of one claim with the authors' explicit agreement statement deciding success. Eligibility itself is the main doubt: a coder could treat Exp 1 as a new experiment (pup-separation question) rather than a replication. DOI not given in the paper, left blank. Author first names not given (initials only). Exp 2 (VEH-1+MK212 vs VEH-1+VEH, fewer pups retrieved, p = 0.014) also reproduces the effect but is not framed as a replication, so not coded.

effects.original_title: Effects of 5-hydroxytryptamine 2C receptor agonist MK212 and 2A receptor antagonist MDL100907 on maternal behavior in postpartum female rats
effects.original_authors: Chen, W; Zhang, Q; Su, W; Zhang, H; Yang, Y; Qiao, J; Sui, N; Li, M
effects.description: Acute systemic administration of the selective 5-HT2C agonist MK212 disrupts maternal behavior, especially pup retrieval, in postpartum rats (2.0 mg/kg producing the most disruption).
effects.citation_sentence: This dose was chosen based on our previous work showing that acute injection of MK212 dose-dependently disrupts rat maternal performance with 2.0 mg/kg MK212 having the most disruption (Chen et al., 2014). ... Behaviorally, we replicated the acute disruptive effect of MK212 on pup retrieval.
effects.evidence: Results 3.4: 'Behaviorally, we replicated the acute disruptive effect of MK212 on pup retrieval. In addition, we found that repeated MK212 treatment produced a persistent disruption of pup retrieval (all p < 0.05) (Figure 6A)'; main effect of drug F(1, 10) = 39.205, p < 0.001 across the 4 test days.
effects.notes: Separate group of 23 postpartum rats (new animals), so a separate replication study from Exp 1. The citation sentence joins two non-adjacent sentences (Methods 2.7 cites Chen et al., 2014; Results 3.4 says 'we replicated' without repeating the citation). The acute behavioral comparison is presumably the first day (PP 6) of the repeated-treatment groups, since the 'acute' groups were not injected during PP 6-9 behavior tests (Methods 2.7); the paper does not report a separate statistic for that day. The repeated-dosing persistence is a new finding, not part of this entry. Eligibility is borderline for the same reason as Exp 1 (incidental self-replication inside a new c-Fos study).
